findings.evidence: Mathlib tags the position of the distinguished argument: `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Orthogonal.lean:63,66` `isOrtho_zero_left`/`isOrtho_zero_right`; the file itself follows that convention for `minkowskiProduct_axisVector_left` (line 329), after Physlib's `minkowskiProduct_basis_left`.
findings.fix: Tag the position of the named vector: `bilinForm_nPlus_right_eq_zero_of_mem_transverse`, `bilinForm_nMinus_right_eq_zero_of_mem_transverse`, `mem_transverse_iff_bilinForm_right_eq_zero` (or equivalent).
findings.issue: `bilinForm_nPlus_eq_zero_of_mem_transverse` (`B w L.nPlus = 0`), `bilinForm_nMinus_eq_zero_of_mem_transverse` (line 272) and `mem_transverse_iff_bilinForm_eq_zero` (line 259) record no argument order, yet the order is their entire content: the opposite statements `B L.nPlus w = 0` / `B L.nMinus w = 0` are the `mem_transverse_iff` direction and would claim the same names.

findings.evidence: Naming addendum: "`_apply`: evaluates a function or bundled map at an argument"; cf. `Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/Spaces/ContinuousLinearMap.lean:362` `toBilinForm_apply`. The specialised-argument lemmas (`plus_nPlus` etc.) correctly need no `_apply` since the argument is named.
findings.issue: `minkowskiAxis_plus (i) (v) : (minkowskiAxis i).plus v = …` and `minkowskiAxis_minus` (line 385) evaluate a bundled linear map at a generic argument but omit `_apply`, so the names advertise an equation between the maps themselves; the same shape is named `plus_apply`/`minus_apply` at lines 115-119 of this file.

findings.evidence: Line 46 vs `finrank_longitudinal : finrank K L.longitudinal = 2` (line 305) and `finrank_transverse_minkowskiProduct_add_one` (line 407), which require the pair to be a proper subspace for `d > 1`.
findings.fix: Write "the standard light-cone basis `(n₊, n₋)`, `n± = (e₀ ± eᵢ)/√2`, of Minkowski space", matching the declaration's own docstring at line 344.
findings.issue: The Main-definitions entry calls `minkowskiAxis i` "the standard basis `n± = (e₀ ± eᵢ)/√2` of Minkowski space". It is a pair of light-like vectors, not a basis of `Vector d` (dimension `d + 1`); the file itself proves the span is only two-dimensional (`finrank_longitudinal`, line 305).

summary: Names and (absent) notation are largely conventional, but three lemma names fail to pin down their statements: the right-argument orthogonality lemmas carry no position tag, and the Minkowski component lemmas drop the `_apply` suffix used by their own general counterparts. One docstring also calls a pair of vectors "the standard basis of Minkowski space".
